attacks.claim: Offline expiry only catches a device clock set earlier than the download time. A clock set back to any point after download but before real time passes `valid_until` will show an expired forecast in color, which breaks the agreed rule against presenting stale safety information as current.
attacks.evidence: "if the device clock reads earlier than that, the stored forecast is treated as expired" (QA tests only 'clock moved earlier than offline download time')

attacks.claim: Forecasts can be superseded by the center before `valid_until`. During a WADE outage the API keeps serving the old rating in color until `valid_until`, so a raised danger rating may never reach the user. Nothing in the design limits this to the 30-minute alert window.
attacks.evidence: "our API keeps serving forecasts still inside `valid_until`"; staging test: "valid forecasts served"

attacks.claim: CDN caching is not tied to `valid_until`. A cached response can keep a zone colored after its forecast expires, unless the CDN TTL is capped at the remaining validity. The 92% hit-rate assumption makes this a likely path.
attacks.evidence: "serves zone geometry + ratings from our CDN"; "92% CDN hit rate"; no CDN TTL stated

attacks.claim: Coloring zones by the highest of three band ratings is a derived rating the centers did not issue, which may conflict with the agreement's ban on altering ratings. The legal review (LGL-902) covers card text and terms only, not this rule.
attacks.evidence: "The zone color uses the highest of the three"; "may not alter ratings or forecast text"; "Card text and the terms-of-use update were reviewed by legal (LGL-902)"

attacks.claim: Removing a center does not stop its display. Offline copies keep showing that center's ratings until each `valid_until`, which may be a day or more. This is a problem if a center has asked to be removed, which the artifact itself anticipates.
attacks.evidence: "(e.g. if a center asks us to stop); its zones disappear within 10 min and any offline copies expire at their `valid_until`"

attacks.claim: The rollback relies on remote config reaching the device. Phones that are offline in the field, or that do not foreground, keep stored forecasts and the layer after rollback, so the claim that no stale ratings remain is overstated.
attacks.evidence: "takes effect on next app foreground"; "so no stale ratings remain on phones"

attacks.claim: The request sends the visible map viewport as `bbox` alongside the client IP, and analytics events carry zone ids. Together these reveal where users are looking and are linkable over time. The artifact gives no retention period for request logs or analytics.
attacks.evidence: "GET /avy/v1/zones?bbox=…"; "rate limited at origin ... per IP"; "Analytics adds two events ... with zone id only" (no retention stated)

attacks.claim: No production monitor checks that served ratings match WADE. Accuracy was verified only by a pre-release 3-day manual comparison, so a parser or band-mapping regression after launch would go unnoticed until someone reports it.
attacks.evidence: "Dashboard: WADE poll success, last update per center, endpoint 5xx and p95, CDN hit rate, crash-free sessions" (no rating-accuracy check)

attacks.claim: `bbox` has no stated maximum area or precision. Arbitrary bboxes can trigger expensive queries and fragment the cache, which undermines the 92% hit-rate assumption.
The cost estimate covers origin only. CDN egress and request cost are not estimated, and the $400 alert is set without a projection to compare against.
A 120 req/min per-IP limit can throttle legitimate users behind shared NAT, such as ski lodges, resorts, or group trips, causing blank zones.
attacks.evidence: "rate limited at origin to 120 req/min per IP"

attacks.claim: The time zone for issue time, valid-until, and "Forecast expired [time]" is not specified. Centers span several zones and the device may be elsewhere, so the displayed times can be misread.
attacks.evidence: "the issue time, the valid-until time"; "Forecast expired [time]" (no time zone)

attacks.claim: The source of the "Read the full forecast" link is not stated, and no scheme or domain allowlist is mentioned. If the URL comes from feed data, a malformed value could open an unintended target.
attacks.evidence: ""Read the full forecast" linking to the center's page" (link source and validation absent)

attacks.claim: WADE is the sole data source for the whole layer, and no exit plan is documented if the contract ends or the feed changes. The layer would then go dark or need an emergency rebuild.
attacks.evidence: "using forecasts published by the regional avalanche centers in the Western Avalanche Data Exchange (WADE)"; "WADE data agreement signed 2026-09-30 (contract C-2209)"

attacks.claim: The center list is duplicated in the config file and the blog post, and the count "19" is hard-coded in the copy. Changing or removing a center requires coordinated edits in two places.
attacks.evidence: "list in `config/avy_centers.json`, same list in the blog post"
